newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian govt, regions at odds over Eurobond issues.
newsitem.headline: Russian govt, regions at odds over Eurobond issues.

text.p: Russia's federal and regional authorities are at odds over how regional Eurobonds should be issued, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.

"There are differences in opinion in the approach of the regions, including Moscow and Nizhny Novgorod, and the federal government to the practice of Eurobond issues," cabinet spokesman Igor Shabdurasulov told a news conference.
He could not provide details, but said the quarrels were hindering the issuance of a government regulation outlining regional Eurobond issues.
First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin has said regional Eurobonds would not be subject to a 15 percent tax on government securities or to a 0.8 percent registration tax.
He also called for restricting Eurobond issues to 30 percent of any given regional budget's annual revenues. Servicing the paper should not exceed 15 percent of a region's revenues.
Several Russian regions and cities, including Moscow, St Petersburg and Nizhny Novgorod, are preparing Eurobond issues, but the launch is delayed by the lack of clarity in the Russian legislation.
